o1.biggest_strength: Dissects the 4.0 ROAS against the 2.5 break-even immediately and clearly isolates non-brand search into dedicated campaigns for the winning themes.
o1.biggest_mistake: Does not explicitly warn the executive team that cutting unprofitable spend will cause top-line reported revenue to dip initially.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add accountability owners and 'done when' completion criteria to the first-week roadmap.

o2.biggest_strength: Combines fearless commercial honesty about the impending top-line dip with an actionable delegation table and a disciplined regional holdout test for brand-building broad spend.
o2.biggest_mistake: Holding back $104,000 in reserve may be slightly too conservative for a 30-day window without an accelerated weekly deployment trigger.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Specify exact campaign targets for non-brand search capture rather than relying solely on feed-only PMax.

reason: Both are masterclasses in retail media buying that nail every number and brand nuance, but Output 2 wins because it proactively warns me that top-line revenue will drop 13%, designs an incremental geo-split test to check if broad spend actually drives assisted brand conversions, and formats the week-one roadmap with explicit owners and completion criteria.
